result:
I would permanently sever the human capacity to dehumanize. 

I would rewire the cognitive disconnect that allows any person—or crowd, or nation—to look at another living being and categorize them as an abstract concept, an obstacle, a monster, or a number. 

No one would ever lose the ability to inherently recognize the fragile, conscious reality of the person standing in front of them, across a border, or on the other side of an argument. You would still have anger, disagreements, and the full spectrum of human emotion. You could still hate. But you would never be able to forget that the target of your hatred feels pain, fears death, and hopes for a good day exactly as deeply as you do.

I would choose this because every systemic cruelty, every war, every atrocity, and every exploitation in human history required the perpetrators to first stop seeing their victims as human. If that switch could never be turned off, every ideology, religion, and government would be forced to exist within the boundaries of radical empathy. It would violently collapse the mechanics of greed and destruction.
